This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

class Tok:
    __slots__=('t','v','line','file')
    def __init__(self,t,v,line,file=""): self.t=t; self.v=v; self.line=line; self.file=file
    def __repr__(self): return f"Tok({self.t},{self.v!r},{self.line})"

def lex_file(src, filename):
    toks=[]
    i=0; line=1; n=len(src)
    in_php=False
    start_line=1
    while i<n:
        if not in_php:
            # find <?
            j=src.find('<?',i)
            if j==-1:
                text=src[i:]; 
                if text: toks.append(Tok('INLINE',text,line,filename))
                break
            if j>i:
                text=src[i:j]; toks.append(Tok('INLINE',text,line,filename)); line+=text.count('\n'); i=j
            # check tag
            if src.startswith('<?=',i):
                toks.append(Tok('OPEN_ECHO','<?=',line,filename)); i+=3; in_php=True
            elif src.startswith('<?php',i) and (i+5>=n or src[i+5] in ' \t\r\n'):
                toks.append(Tok('OPEN','<?php',line,filename)); i+=5; in_php=True
            elif src.startswith('<?',i) and not src.startswith('<?xml',i):
                toks.append(Tok('OPEN','<?',line,filename)); i+=2; in_php=True
            else:
                # literal <?
                toks.append(Tok('INLINE','<?',line,filename)); i+=2
        else:
            # php mode
            if src.startswith('?>',i):
                toks.append(Tok('CLOSE','?>',line,filename)); i+=2; in_php=False
                # swallow one newline
                if src.startswith('\r\n',i): i+=2; line+=1
                elif i<n and src[i]=='\n': i+=1; line+=1
                continue

            if c=='\n': line+=1; i+=1; continue
            if c in ' \t\r': i+=1; continue
            if src.startswith('//',i) or c=='#':
                # comment to end line or ?>
                j=src.find('\n',i)
                k=src.find('?>',i)
                if k!=-1 and (j==-1 or k<j):
                    i=k; continue
                if j==-1: i=n; break
                i=j; continue
            if src.startswith('/*',i):
                j=src.find('*/',i+2)
                if j==-1:

                else:

                    ch=src[j]

                    closing_start = mm.start()+ (1 if src[mm.start()]=='\n' else 0)

                    ls=src.rfind('\n',0,label_pos)+1

            toks.append(Tok('OP',c,line,filename)); i+=1; continue
    toks.append(Tok('EOF',None,line,filename))
    return toks

CONST_DATA=""

def _init_classes(self):
    # Exception hierarchy etc defined in builtins module section via register
    register_core_classes(self)
Interp.init_classes=_init_classes

def _out(self,s):
    if self.output_buffers:
        top=self.output_buffers[-1]
        # top: [buffer_list, callable]
        top[0].append(str(s))
    else:
        try:
            sys.stdout.write(str(s)); sys.stdout.flush()
        except BrokenPipeError:
            pass
Interp.out=_out
def _warning(self,msg,line=None,kind="Warning"):
    if self.quiet: return
    lvl_map={"Warning":2,"Notice":8,"Deprecated":8192,"Fatal error":1}
    # error_reporting check
    lvl=lvl_map.get(kind,2)
    if self.error_reporting_val is not None and not (self.error_reporting_val & lvl):
        return
    file=self.current_file
    ln=line if line is not None else self.current_line
    text=f"\n{kind}: {msg} in {file} on line {ln}\n"
    self.last_error={'type':lvl,'message':msg,'file':file,'line':ln}
    # user handler?
    if self.error_handler:
        try:
            r=self.call_callable(self.error_handler,[lvl,msg,file,ln],line=ln)
            if r is True: return
        except Exception:
            pass
    # display_errors ini: "STDOUT" or "1"/True -> output; "0"/False -> not
    de=self.ini.get('display_errors')
    if de in (False,'0','Off','off',''): return
    self.out(text)
Interp.warning=_warning
def _notice(self,msg,line=None): self.warning(msg,line,"Notice")
def _deprecated(self,msg,line=None): self.warning(msg,line,"Deprecated")
Interp.notice=_notice; Interp.deprecated=_deprecated

def _obj_to_string(self,obj,line=0):
    # enum?
    cd=self.classes.get(obj.cls.lower())
    # find __toString
    m=self.find_method(obj.cls,'__toString')
    if m:
        try:
            r=self.call_method(obj,'__toString',[],line=line)
            return to_string(r,self,line)
        except ThrowExc as e:
            raise
    if obj.cls.lower()=='stdclass':
        self.fatal_error(f"Object of class stdClass could not be converted to string",line,obj=obj)
    # enum case name?
    if cd and cd.kind=='enum':
        # UnitEnum cases have name prop, but to string error in PHP
        self.fatal_error(f"Object of class {obj.cls} could not be converted to string",line)
    self.fatal_error(f"Object of class {obj.cls} could not be converted to string",line)
    return obj.cls
Interp.obj_to_string=_obj_to_string

def _fatal_error(self,msg,line=None,obj=None):
    # create Error object ?
    raise FatalExc(msg,obj,line or self.current_line)
Interp.fatal_error=_fatal_error

def _find_class(self,name):
    if not isinstance(name,str): return None
    key=name.lstrip('\\').lower()
    if key in self.classes: return self.classes[key]
    # alias?
    return None
def _class_exists_check(self,name):
    return _find_class(self,name) is not None
Interp.find_class=_find_class

def _find_method(self,cls_name,method):
    if not cls_name: return None
    cd=_find_class(self,cls_name)
    seen=set()
    while cd:
        if cd.name.lower() in seen: break
        seen.add(cd.name.lower())
        if method.lower() in cd.methods: return cd.methods[method.lower()]
        # traits already merged into methods at declaration
        if cd.parent: cd=_find_class(self,cd.parent)
        else: break
    return None
Interp.find_method=_find_method

def _is_subclass(self,child,parent):
    if not child or not parent: return False
    cl=child.lower(); pl=parent.lower()
    if cl==pl: return True
    cd=_find_class(self,child)
    seen=set()
    while cd:
        if cd.parent and cd.parent.lower()==pl: return True
        for iface in cd.interfaces:
            if iface.lower()==pl: return True
            # interface extends interface (stored as parent for interfaces)
            if _is_subclass(self,iface,parent): return True
        if cd.parent:
            if cd.parent.lower()==pl: return True
            cd=_find_class(self,cd.parent)
        else: break
    return False
Interp.is_subclass=_is_subclass
